# Volume 2 — XII A Jonah Day

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The previous evening actually marked the start of it, marked by a fitful, sleepless night of throbbing tooth pain. As Nell got out of bed in the gloomy, biting winter dawn, she was consumed by a sense that existence was dull, weary, and useless.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0000 }

She was in a far from angelic mood as she went to school. Her face was aching and her cheek had swollen. Because the fire refused to burn, the schoolroom was smoky and cold, and the children were gathered around it in shivering groups. With a tone sharper than any she had used before, Nell sent them to their seats. Anthony Tulk strutted to his with the impertinent swagger he usually had, and she saw him whisper a remark to his seat-mate before looking at her with a grin.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0001 }

It appeared to Nell that the number of squeaking pencils that morning exceeded anything she had ever experienced; furthermore, as Barbara Shaw approached the desk carrying an arithmetic problem, she stumbled over the coal scuttle with catastrophic consequences. Coal scattered across all areas of the room, her slate shattered into pieces, and upon standing back up, her coal-dust-streaked face caused the boys to burst into loud laughter.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0002 }

Nell turned away from the class of second readers that she was listening to.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0003 }

“Honestly, Barbara,” she remarked with coldness, “you should stay in your chair if you are unable to walk without tripping over an object. A young woman of your years acting with such clumsiness is utterly shameful.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0004 }

Stumbling back to her desk, poor Barbara saw her tears mix with the coal dust, creating a truly grotesque appearance. Such a tone and manner had never before been used toward her by her cherished, empathetic teacher, leaving Barbara heartbroken. A pang of guilt touched Nell herself, though it merely heightened her inner annoyance, and that particular lesson remains in the memory of the second reader class to this day, alongside the ruthless dose of arithmetic that came after. At the very moment Nell was sharply issuing the sums, St. Clair Trask arrived out of breath.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0005 }

“St. Clair, you have arrived thirty minutes behind schedule,” Nell informed him with a cold tone. “What caused this?”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0006 }

“Please, miss, I had to help ma make a pudding for dinner ’cause we’re expecting company and Clarice Almira’s sick,” replied St. Clair, speaking in a completely polite tone that nonetheless amused his classmates immensely.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0007 }

“Take your seat and work out the six problems on page eighty-four of your arithmetic for punishment,” Nell said. Her tone left St. Clair looking somewhat astonished, yet he proceeded submissively to his desk and pulled out his slate. After that, he surreptitiously handed a tiny package over the aisle to Joe Mott. Spotting him as he did it, Nell arrived at a disastrous assumption regarding the package.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0008 }

An addition to her meager earnings had recently been sought by old Mrs. Hiram Mott through the baking and vending of “nut cakes.” These confections held a particular appeal for young boys, causing Nell a good deal of difficulty over the preceding few weeks. While traveling to school, the boys were accustomed to spending their extra money at Mrs. Hiram’s shop, carrying the confections to the schoolhouse with them, and, whenever feasible, consuming them and sharing them with their friends throughout the class day. Though Nell had cautioned them that future cakes brought into the schoolhouse would be taken away, St. Clair Trask was nevertheless casually handing over a package of the treats, encased in the blue and white striped paper that Mrs. Hiram employed, directly in front of her.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0009 }

“Joseph,” Nell said in a low voice, “hand me that package.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0010 }

Shaken and embarrassed, Joe complied. That chubby child invariably turned red and stumbled over his words whenever fear struck him. At that instance, no person could have possibly appeared more blameworthy than unfortunate Joe.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0011 }

“Cast it into the flames,” Nell said.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0012 }

Joe’s expression became extremely blank.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0013 }

“M . . . m . . . miss, p . . . p . . . p . . . lease,” he started.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0014 }

“Follow my instructions, Joseph, and do not speak a word regarding it.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0015 }

“B . . . b . . . but m . . . m . . . miss . . . th . . . th . . . those people are . . .” Joe stammered out, completely overwhelmed.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0016 }

“Joseph, will you do as I command or will you refuse?” inquired Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0017 }

A boy less daring and confident than Joe Mott would have felt intimidated by her demeanor and the perilous gleam in her eyes. None of her students had previously witnessed this altered version of Nell. Casting a desperate look toward St. Clair, Joe walked over to the stove, pulled open its large, rectangular front door, and tossed the blue and white package inside, moving faster than St. Clair—who had leaped up—could speak. He then leaped backward barely in time.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0018 }

For a brief time, the frightened inhabitants of Brierley school could not tell if the event was an earthquake or an eruption of a volcano. The harmless-appearing package that Nell had hastily assumed held Mrs. Hiram’s nut cakes actually contained a collection of pinwheels and firecrackers which Warren Mott had requested St. Clair Trask’s father to bring from town the previous day, planning a birthday party for that night. The firecrackers detonated with a booming roar, and the pinwheels, shooting through the doorway, whirled wildly about the space while spluttering and hissing. Nell collapsed onto her seat, pale from shock, and every girl scrambled onto her desk with loud screams. Joe Mott remained frozen like a statue amidst the chaos, while St. Clair, overwhelmed by amusement, swayed back and forth in the aisle. Prillie Rogerson lost consciousness, and Annetta Bell broke into hysterics.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0019 }

A few minutes passed, though it felt like a lengthy duration, prior to the final pinwheel dying down. Once she regained her composure, Nell rushed to unseal the doors and windows to release the smoke and gas that pervaded the space. Following that, she assisted the girls in transporting the insensible Prillie to the porch, at which point Barbara Shaw, desperate to render aid, dumped a bucket of nearly icy water across Prillie's shoulders and face before anyone had a chance to prevent her.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0020 }

An entire hour passed before calm returned once more . . . yet it was a stillness that could almost be sensed physically. Everyone understood that the teacher’s mood remained uncleared, despite the outburst. Except for Anthony Tulk, no one ventured to utter a whisper. While solving an arithmetic problem, Ned Clay made his pencil squeak by mistake, met Nell’s gaze, and desired nothing more than for the ground to split apart and consume him. The continent was rushed through by the geography class at a pace that left them reeling. Within an inch of their lives, the grammar class members were parsed and analyzed. When Chester Mott spelled “odoriferous” using a pair of f’s, he was forced to realize that he would never overcome the shame of his error, whether in the present life or the one to follow.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0021 }

Nell was aware of the absurdity of her actions and that people would jest about the event at numerous tea-tables that evening, yet this awareness merely heightened her fury. Had she been less agitated, she might have laughed the matter off, but such a reaction was currently out of the question; consequently, she paid it no heed with frozen contempt.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0022 }

Upon Nell’s return to the school following dinner, the pupils were seated as always, each head bowed diligently above a desk with the sole exception of Anthony Tulk’s. From over his book, he stared toward Nell, his dark eyes shimmering with inquisitiveness and derision. Nell yanked the drawer of her desk open to look for chalk, whereupon a energetic mouse jumped from the drawer right beneath her hand, scurried across the desk, and dropped to the floor.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0023 }

Nell shrieked and leapt backward, as though she had encountered a serpent, while Anthony Tulk burst into open laughter.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0024 }

After that, a quiet descended . . . an exceedingly eerie, uneasy quiet. Annetta Bell wavered between surrendering to another fit of hysterics or refraining, particularly because she was uncertain about the exact location of the mouse. However, she chose against it. How could anyone derive any solace from hysterics when faced with a teacher whose countenance was so pale and whose eyes burned so intensely?
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0025 }

“Who put that mouse in my desk?” asked Nell. Although she spoke in a rather quiet tone, it sent a tremble along Cedric Stanhope’s backbone. Joe Mott met her gaze and felt guilty from his head down to his feet, yet he babbled out erratically,
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0026 }

“I . . . i . . . isn’t m . . . m . . . my f . . . f . . . fault instructor, i . . . i . . . isn’t m . . . m . . . my f . . . f . . . fault.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0027 }

Ignoring the miserable Joseph, Nell directed her gaze toward Anthony Tulk, who returned her look without any shame or embarrassment.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0028 }

“Anthony, did you do that?”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0029 }

“Indeed, it was,” Anthony answered in an insolent manner.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0030 }

Nell removed her long, heavy pointer made of hardwood from her desk.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0031 }

“Anthony, come here.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0032 }

This was by no means the harshest penalty Anthony Tulk had ever experienced. Nell, despite the tempestuous state of her soul right then, was incapable of inflicting cruel punishment on any youngster. Nevertheless, the pointer bit sharp enough that Anthony’s defiance ultimately gave way; he shrank back as tears filled his eyes.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0033 }

Full of remorse, Nell let go of the pointer and instructed Anthony to return to his place. Ashamed, penitent, and deeply embarrassed, she took her seat at her desk. Now that her swift temper had vanished, she desperately wished she could find comfort through weeping. This was the result of all her bragging . . . she had physically struck a student. Odette was going to gloat so much! Furthermore, Mr. Pettifer was going to laugh heartily! Yet even more painful than those prospects, and the most agonizing realization of all, was that her final opportunity to earn the affection of Anthony Tulk was gone. From this point on, he would never care for her.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0034 }

Nell, through what has been termed "a Herculaneum effort," held her tears at bay until arriving at her home that evening. At that point, she locked herself inside the east gable room and poured all her shame, remorse, and disappointment into her pillows as she wept . . . weeping for such a duration that Thirza became frightened, entered the room, and demanded to discover the nature of the problem.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0035 }

“My conscience is bothering me,” weeping, Nell confessed. “Oh, Thirza, today has been an absolute jinx. I feel so embarrassed by my behavior. Anthony Tulk got whipped because I lost my temper.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0036 }

“That pleases me,” Thirza declared firmly. “You ought to have taken this action a long time since.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0037 }

“Oh, no, no, Thirza. And I fail to understand how I can ever face those children again. It feels as though I have degraded myself completely into the dust. You cannot imagine how irritable and spiteful and terrible I was. The look in Cedric Stanhope’s eyes is something I am unable to forget . . . such surprise and disappointment were on his face. Oh, Thirza, my efforts to remain patient and to gain Anthony’s affection have been so great . . . and now everything has been utterly wasted.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0038 }

With an extraordinary gentleness, Thirza ran her rough, labor-calloused hand through the young woman's shiny, disheveled locks. As the weeping of Nell began to subside, she remarked, with a softness unusual for her,
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0039 }

“Nell, you interpret matters far too deeply. Errors are committed by everyone . . . yet folks dismiss them from memory. Furthermore, periods of bad luck happen to each person. Regarding Anthony Tulk, what reason is there for you to mind if he holds a grudge against you? No one else feels that way.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0040 }

“It is beyond my control. My desire is for everyone to hold me dear, so whenever someone fails to, it causes me great pain. Now, Anthony certainly never will. Oh, today I simply acted like a fool, Thirza. Every detail will be revealed to you.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0041 }

Thirza paid attention to the entire narrative, without Nell ever knowing whether she smiled at particular moments. Once the story had been concluded, she remarked in a brisk tone,
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0042 }

“Oh, don't worry about it. Today is finished, and a fresh day arrives tomorrow that contains no errors as of yet, just as you were accustomed to saying. Simply step down to the lower floor and eat your evening meal. You will discover whether or not a warm mug of tea along with the plum puffs that I baked today will raise your spirits.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0043 }

“Plum puffs won’t minister to a mind diseased,” Nell remarked mournfully; Thirza, however, viewed it as a positive indication that her recovery allowed her to modify a quote.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0044 }

The lively dinner table, featuring the radiant expressions of the twins, along with the peerless plum puffs made by Thirza . . . four of which were consumed by Robin . . . managed to “hearten her up” quite a bit despite everything. Having slept well during the night, she woke up when morning arrived to discover that both she and her surroundings were completely changed. Throughout the dark hours, snow had fallen quietly and heavily, and the lovely white blanket, sparkling under the cold sunlight, appeared to be a cloak of forgiveness draped over every error and embarrassment of yesterday.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0045 }

“Each morning brings a new start, Each morning the world is created anew,”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0046 }

“sang Nell, as she dressed.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0047 }

Because of the snow, she was forced to take the long way by the road to get to school, and she considered it a truly mischievous twist of fate that Anthony Tulk happened to come trudging past right at the moment she emerged from the Grey Shutters lane. She experienced as much guilt as though they had swapped places; nevertheless, to her immense surprise, Anthony did not merely raise his cap . . . an action he had failed to perform ever before . . . but remarked casually,
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0048 }

“Walking’s a bit rough, isn’t it? Would you like me to carry those books, teacher?”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0049 }

Nell gave up her volumes and questioned whether she could actually be conscious. Anthony continued walking toward the school without speaking, yet as Nell received her volumes she beamed down at him . . . not the mechanical “kind” beam she had so continuously put on for his sake but an abrupt radiance of genuine fellowship. Anthony beamed . . . no, to be entirely honest, Anthony smirked in return. A smirk is not usually considered to be a polite gesture; nevertheless Nell abruptly sensed that even if she had not yet gained Anthony’s affection she had, one way or another, gained his respect.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0050 }

This was affirmed by Mrs. Agatha Sowerby when she arrived on the following Saturday.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0051 }

“Well, Nell, I suppose Anthony Tulk has been won over by you, and that is the truth. He claims he now thinks you have some worth, despite being a girl. He remarks that the beating he received from you was ‘just as good as a man’s.’”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0052 }

“However, beating him was something I did not anticipate would earn his favor,” Nell remarked with a touch of sadness, sensing that her principles had somehow let her down. “This feels incorrect. My belief in gentle treatment must be correct, I am certain.”
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0053 }

“No, but the Tulks break every established rule, that’s the point,” asserted Mrs. Agatha with certainty.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0054 }

Upon hearing this, Mr. Pettifer remarked, “Thought you’d come to it,” and Odette emphasized the point in a somewhat pitiless manner.
{: #nw-v02-c12-p0055 }
